jurisdiction.name: Luxembourg
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Luxembourg governs AI mainly through EU law plus national policy: its May 2025 AI strategy (replacing the 2019 strategy), the data protection authority's (CNPD) AI regulatory sandbox launched in 2024, and the financial regulator (CSSF) and central bank's thematic reviews of AI in finance. Bill 8476 implementing the EU AI Act, which would make the CNPD the default authority and coordinator, was still in parliamentary committee in October 2026, and the education ministry proposed an AI framework for schools in 2025.
lead_institutions: Ministry of State (Media, Connectivity and Digital Policy)
Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. Luxembourg's law implementing the EU AI Act is still a bill and is listed as a lead, and the 2019 strategy could only be located. Guidelines for AI use in the central administration are listed as a lead because they carry no publication date.

instruments.official_title: La stratégie du Luxembourg en matière d'intelligence artificielle (Accélérer la souveraineté numérique 2030)
instruments.issuing_authority: Government of Luxembourg: Ministry of State, Ministry of Higher Education and Research, Ministry of the Economy and Ministry for Digitalisation
instruments.current_status: Presented by the government on 19 May 2025, with an official English version ('Luxembourg's AI Strategy'); it is in force as the current strategy, with a budget horizon of 2025-2030.
instruments.summary: Luxembourg's national AI strategy to 2030, one of three aligned strategies (data, AI, quantum) under 'Accélérer la souveraineté numérique 2030', prepared by the Ministry of State, the research, economy and digitalisation ministries. It sets 30 actions across six levers (talent and skills, infrastructure, services, R&D and innovation, governance and regulation, international cooperation), high-impact sectors (public administration, finance, health, culture) and flagship projects such as the 4LM legal large language model and a sovereign educational chatbot. On governance it backs a pragmatic AI Act implementation through bill 8476 (decentralised model with the CNPD as default market surveillance authority and coordinator) and implementation of the Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current national AI strategy; replaces the 2019 strategic vision and frames AI Act implementation and public-sector AI.

instruments.english_title: Sandkëscht - CNPD regulatory sandbox (AI and data protection)
instruments.current_status: Running; programme page last updated 30/06/2025. Launch announced by the CNPD on 21 May 2024. Bill 8476 (AI Act implementation, pending) would give the CNPD a role regarding AI regulatory sandboxes under the AI Act.
instruments.summary: The CNPD's 'Sandkëscht' regulatory sandbox, launched on 21 May 2024 with applications from 14 June 2024, lets organisations established in Luxembourg test AI systems and new uses of personal data with CNPD support for a limited period before market launch. Participation follows a project-specific plan built on five principles (proactivity, collaboration, experimentation, agility, results) and a participation charter the participant must accept; the programme is grounded in the CNPD's GDPR awareness mission (Article 57(1)(d)) and focuses on GDPR compliance.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: National AI regulatory sandbox run by the data protection authority; cited in the 2025 AI strategy.

instruments.current_status: In force (as amended); published in Mémorial A n° 686 on 16 August 2018 (law dated 1 August 2018). Short citation title: 'Loi du 1er août 2018 portant organisation de la Commission nationale pour la protection des données et du régime général sur la protection des données'. Pending bills 8476 (AI Act) and 8464 (Convention 108+ protocol) would amend it.
instruments.summary: Luxembourg's national GDPR implementing law: it organises the CNPD as independent supervisory authority, defines its powers and sanctions, and sets national rules within the GDPR's margins (e.g. on employment-related processing via the Labour Code). It governs the processing of personal data used to train and run AI systems in Luxembourg and is the law that bill 8476 would amend to give the CNPD its AI Act tasks.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General data protection law applying to AI training and use; basis of the CNPD's AI-related role.

instruments.official_title: Proposition d'un cadre stratégique de l'intelligence artificielle à l'école (KI Kompass)
instruments.english_title: Proposed strategic framework for artificial intelligence in schools (KI Kompass)
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Education, Children and Youth
instruments.current_status: Presented on 6 October 2025 as a proposal to be discussed with school partners in consultation meetings. An adapted final framework had not been found on official sites by 12 October 2026.
instruments.summary: Education ministry's proposed framework for responsible AI, including generative AI, in Luxembourg schools, built on a survey of 4,000 pupils and 200 teachers. It sets a progressive approach (learning without AI in primary school, learning about AI in lower secondary, learning with AI in upper secondary, more autonomous use from 16), the AI competences pupils should acquire, and rules on academic integrity, practical classroom directives, prohibitions and sanctions, and the limits of AI detectors. It comes with a platform giving teachers and pupils secure access to ministry-validated AI tools.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Luxembourg's legislation portal, parliament, government, ministries and regulators were searched. No AI-specific law is in force, and no material was found for risk and assurance, procurement, cybersecurity, standards or international instruments; the AI Act implementing bill and the central-administration AI guidelines, which state no publication date, are listed as leads. The financial regulator's 2018 AI white paper, the text of the 2019 AI strategy and the date of the central-administration guidelines remain to be checked.
